title: Finite coefficient dimension makes derived global sections preserve coproducts
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring and X a qcqs scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Suppose a uniform integer d bounds H^q(X,M)=0 for every Λ-module sheaf M and q>d, in the sense of HasFiniteCohomologicalDimension Λ X. Then unbounded RΓ(X,-) [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor] preserves coproducts indexed by every type in the coefficient universe, including the empty type.

source.place: Stacks Tag 0F11 part (2), for arbitrary coefficient rings with a uniform dimension bound

proof.text: Reuse the proved source theorem, with no finite-cardinality hypothesis on Λ. On a qcqs scheme all classical higher global sections preserve coproducts by filtered colimits of finite subsums. The single-sheaf comparison transfers the given unbounded bound to classical derived functors, replacing d by max(d,0). The source acyclic-term complex theorem computes the unbounded right derived functor on sums of injective-term resolutions. Its preservation theorem transports the termwise coproduct cocone through the canonical unit comparisons. This gives the canonical derived coproduct, including the empty family.
